subject: storytime
title: Jack and the Beanstalk
about: The English folk tale of the boy who trades his cow for five magic beans, climbs the beanstalk to a giant's castle and brings home the hen that lays golden eggs. First graders love the climb, the chant of fee, fi, fo, fum and chopping down the beanstalk, and the story is a good one for talking about brave choices and careful trades. In this softened telling nobody is hurt and the giant simply stays grumbling up in the clouds; it is a public-domain story retold in first-grade words, five pages long.
tip: Ask: was one old cow for five beans a good trade, and how did it turn out in the end?

book.author: a folk tale from England (retold)
book.source: public domain, retold in first-grade words
book.blurb: Five magic beans, one tall beanstalk, and a grumpy giant.

passage.text:
Once there was a boy named Jack.
He lived with his mother.
They were very poor.
All they had was one old cow.
"Take the cow to market," said his mother.
"Sell her for some money."
On the way, Jack met a man.
"I will trade you for that cow," said the man.
"Five magic beans!"
So Jack made the trade.
***
"Beans?" said his mother.
"Oh, Jack! We needed that money."
She tossed the beans out the window.
In the night, the beans began to grow.
They grew and grew and grew.
In the morning, Jack saw a giant beanstalk.
It went up, up, up into the clouds!
Jack climbed it to the very top.
***
At the top was a huge castle.
Jack crept inside.
"Fee, fi, fo, fum!" boomed a giant.
"I smell a boy!"
He was big and grumpy.
Jack hid behind a big pot.
The giant sat down.
"Hen, lay!" he said.
A little hen laid a golden egg.
Jack knew that hen!
She was his family's hen.
The giant had taken her long ago.
***
Soon the giant fell asleep.
Jack tiptoed out.
He picked up the hen.
"Come home with me," he whispered.
Then he ran for the beanstalk.
"Cluck!" said the hen.
The giant woke up.
"Who took my hen?" he roared.
Jack climbed down as fast as he could.
The giant looked down.
The beanstalk was much too thin for him.
***
Jack got to the bottom.
"Mother! Get the axe!" he called.
Chop, chop, chop!
Down came the beanstalk.
Far up in the clouds, the giant grumbled.
"Humph!" he said.
He never came down.
Jack gave the hen to his mother.
"She lays golden eggs," he said.
Now they were never poor again.
Be brave, and think before you trade.

cards.q: What did Jack trade the cow for?
cards.note: His mother was upset, because they needed the money, and she tossed the beans out the window.

cards.q: What grew outside the window in the night?
cards.note: The beans grew and grew until the beanstalk reached up into the clouds.

cards.q: What did the little hen lay?
cards.note: Hen, lay, said the giant, and out came a golden egg.

cards.q: What did Jack take from the giant?
cards.note: The hen had been his family's hen all along, and the giant had taken her long ago.

cards.q: What happened first in the story?
cards.note: Everything starts with the trade on the way to market.

cards.q: What happened at the end of the story?
cards.note: Chop, chop, chop, and the giant stayed up in the clouds while Jack and his mother were never poor again.
He booms fee, fi, fo, fum, roars when his hen is gone, and grumbles when he cannot follow.
Be brave, and think before you trade; the last line says it.

cards.q: In the story, what does 'crept' mean?
cards.note: Jack crept into the castle so the giant would not hear him.

cards.q: Which word is in the story?
cards.note: He reads the three words himself; only one of them is in the story.
